rv.q: Director Ramin Gray brings clinical detachment to this shallow comedy about skin-deep beauty
Broken Nose Theatre’s take on The Ugly One left us feeling amused, bemused, and thoughtful.

Segal strike the balance perfectly between innocence and malevolence, as Lette’s newfound power sees him inflict the same injustice he once suffered on his colleague, stealing his ideas and passing them off as his own.

cn.t: Critics find "The Ugly One" a witty, fast-paced provocation on identity and appearance, earning solid praise for its sharp writing and clever staging. A thought-provoking if uneven ride — bold questions, mostly satisfying answers.
